messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Scan1 Poster Presentation Parameters
messages.body_plain:
If you were doing something like:

  png("myplot.png", height=500, width=1000)
  plot(scan1_output, map)
  dev.off()

You could add pointsize=24 or something like that to the call to png() to make all of the text bigger.

  png("myplot.png", height=500, width=1000, pointsize=24)
  plot(scan1_output, map)
  dev.off()

But there are a lot of different approaches to controlling things. If you show a bit of your code and results, we can give further suggestions.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
messages.body_plain:
There are a lot of different options for how you encode the data, but yes for crosstype "risib" you need to code genotypes according to the founders' alleles, and A/B is one choice that could work.

The BXD mouse RIL are one example dataset to look at:

    https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2data/tree/master/BXD

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] plot_snpasso gene label size
messages.body_plain:
Oh, wait; I guess from your subject you are saying that you want to edit the *size* of the gene labels.
I don't think there's an easy way to do that.

There's a lot of work done to lay out those genes so that they don't overlap. The size of the font is basically determined by the number of genes that get shown. To modify that, you pretty much have to make a copy of the plot_genes() function and edit it to do what you want.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
messages.body_plain:
The heatmap plotting function is not so critical as the actual
calculations, which aren't yet available in R/qtl2.
There's nothing to calculate and then transfer back to R/qtl1, at present.

You can try doing genome scans to look for interactions with particular
QTL, by using scan1() with the genotype probabilities for a specific
location as interactive covariates with the intcovar argument. You
could, in principle, repeat that for every location, and
roll-your-own-scan2().

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] RIL fullsib population
messages.body_plain:
You shouldn’t need to rerun scan1(). You just need a physical map that corresponds to the genetic map you used in calc_genoprob(). If you had used insert_pseudomarkers(), then you would need to use interp_map() to get interpolated positions for the pseudomarkers.

lod_int() and bayes_int() take the scan1 output and a map; the map could be genetic or physical positions.

karl
